q: CDP asks how I engage my own suppliers on climate. What can a small supplier honestly say?
title: CDP supplier engagement for a small firm
short: Describe only what you actually do: asking key suppliers for energy or emissions data, adding climate questions to supplier onboarding, or buying lower-carbon inputs. Give the share of suppliers or spend it covers. If you do nothing yet, say so and state the first step you will take.

p: CDP asks whether you engage your value chain on environmental issues, with whom (suppliers, customers, others), how, and how much of your supply base it covers, usually as a share of suppliers or of procurement spend. Engagement ranges from collecting information to setting requirements and working jointly on reductions.

sections.h: Engagement a small supplier can honestly report
ul: Collecting data: you asked your top raw material and freight suppliers for energy use, emissions or product footprints.
Requirements: purchase orders or supplier onboarding forms now include climate or energy questions.
Purchasing choices: you shifted part of a material to recycled content or a supplier with lower-carbon production, with invoices to show it.
Joint work: a project with a supplier, such as returnable packaging or full-truck loads.

ol: List suppliers by annual spend from your purchase register.
Mark those you engaged during the reporting year.
Coverage by spend = spend with engaged suppliers / total procurement spend.
If you engaged 6 suppliers who account for Rs 2.4 crore of Rs 4 crore spend, coverage is 60% of spend.

p: Do not count a supplier as engaged because you sent one email with no reply, and do not describe a plan as something already done. A customer may ask for the evidence.

senseible: Senseible reads purchase invoices and keeps supplier, spend, quantity and HSN code in a separate supplier evidence trail, which gives you the spend list for coverage and the record of what you bought.
